does: Cuts food into even cubes, so that every piece cooks at the same speed.
how: Trim the piece so that it has a flat side and sits still on the board.
Cut it into slabs as thick as the cube you want.
Stack the slabs and cut them into sticks of the same width.
Turn the sticks and cut across them into cubes.
For an onion, halve it through the root, cut towards the root without cutting through it, then slice across.

cues.text: The cubes are all one size, with square edges.
The knife glides forward and down. Your knuckles guide the blade and your fingertips stay tucked behind them.

mistakes.mistake: Pieces of different sizes, so the small ones turn to mush before the large ones are tender.
mistakes.fix: Set the thickness with the first cut. Every later cut copies it.

mistakes.mistake: Chasing a round vegetable that rolls under the knife.
mistakes.fix: Cut a thin slice off one side first and rest it on that flat.

comes_after.why: A dice is a slice cut again, lengthwise and across, so an even slice comes first.
